newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - THURSDAY JULY 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - THURSDAY JULY 3.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-left government on Wednesday opened the second round of talks with union leaders and employers on welfare reform after a shaky start a month ago. The second round is concentrating on how to reduce tax evasion and how to tackle unemployment through proposals to encourage part-time work, reduce the average work week and create jobs in the poorer south (all).

* Stet/Telecom Italia and AT&T Corp announced a strategic global telecoms alliance with a focus on Latin America and Europe. In Europe, Stet/Telecom Italia would join AT&T-Unisource with the option of taking up to 30 percent of AT&T-Unisource. Telecoms Minister Antonio Maccanico said AT&T could become a stable shareholder in Stet once it has been privatised, AT&T managing director John Walter said it was too early to say (all).

* Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani is expected to meet Olivetti's managing director Roberto Colaninno and unions to discuss the situation at Olivetti Personal Computers. Olivetti PC was recently sold to Gottesman's Piedmont International and the U.S. group said it had raised its capitalisation in Olivetti PC to 65 million dollar to be paid by the end of the week (all).

* Gian Maria Gros Pietro, chairman of state industrial holding IRI, said the group had a net-debt of 3.6 trillion lire at end-June. Gros Pietro said the figure met commitments made to the EU on reducing IRI's debt. IRI's head added the group intends to speed up procedures to sell off its holding in Banca di Roma, in which it holds a 13.8 stake (all).

* The board of French media group Canal Plus decided to leave Europe's biggest televion market, Germany, and strengthen the company's position in Italy. Canal Plus said it would sell its 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere and buy a 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepiu' from Kirch (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
